title: Clinical practice guidelines for telesurgery, 2nd Edition
network_focus: Network requirements; latency; jitter; loss; bandwidth; redundancy
main_finding: Guideline states required bandwidth is robot/codec-specific; calls for no large delay/significant jitter/loss; recommends network+new encode/decode processing delay within 100 ms maximum; redundancy should be tested through failure/switch/recovery.
limitation: Consensus/guideline threshold, not a universal physical limit.

title: Expert Consensus-Based Technical Guidelines for Remote Robotic-Assisted Surgery and Procedures
network_focus: Surgical-grade networks; QoS; redundancy; failover; security
main_finding: Defines fundamental requirements for reliable surgical-grade networking and explicitly avoids universal numeric latency/jitter/bandwidth specifications because use cases differ.
limitation: Industry/clinical expert consensus; does not evaluate a single clinical system.

title: Clinical Recommendations for Remote Robotic Assisted Surgery From the CRSA 2025 International Consensus Conference
network_focus: Uptime; bandwidth; latency; jitter; packet loss
main_finding: Consensus recommends 99.999% uptime, guaranteed bandwidth, total teleoperation latency <300 ms and ideally <200 ms, minimal/no jitter and zero/near-zero loss.
limitation: Consensus target differs from Japanese guideline definition; not evidence of one universal safe threshold.

title: A Multidimensional Perspective on Network Conditions in Telesurgery
network_focus: Latency × bandwidth × jitter × packet loss interactions
main_finding: Pilot in-vitro navigation study treats network state as a 4D space; worsening conditions reduced feasibility and performance; latency and packet loss were dominant and interactions were significant.
limitation: In-vitro neurovascular task and system-specific network stack; downstream CV reliability not studied.

title: Tele-assessment of bandwidth limitation for remote robotics surgery
network_focus: Bandwidth; packet loss; image degradation; video compression
main_finding: At 145 Mbps available bandwidth, 3–7% packet loss and visible image degradation occurred; 120-Mbps video setting performed worse than 40/20 Mbps under that constrained condition; authors concluded ≥150 Mbps for their hinotori setup.
limitation: System-specific requirement; video/control/audio overhead and codec settings differ across platforms.

title: Verification of delay time and image compression thresholds for telesurgery
main_finding: Eight robotic surgeons tested 30/50/100/150-ms delay and 120/60/30/20/10-Mbps video; 30–50 ms were rated feasible while 100–150 ms were rated lower; compression down to 10 Mbps remained usable in that setup.
limitation: Subjective/animal-model validation and hinotori-specific encoder; delay definition is experiment-specific.

title: Maximum acceptable communication delay for the realization of telesurgery
main_finding: 34 participants tested 0–300 ms; performance worsened as delay increased; experienced surgeons remained comparable to less-experienced no-delay performance at ≤100 ms in this setup.
limitation: Prototype/simulated tasks; fixed latency with no jitter/loss; ~50 ms encoder/decoder contribution in delayed conditions.

title: Effect of video lag on laparoscopic surgery: correlation between performance and usability at low latencies
venue: International Journal of Medical Robotics and Computer Assisted Surgery 13
main_finding: 15 trainees and 14 surgeons showed significant performance and usability deterioration at 105 ms added video latency; surgeons were more negatively affected.
limitation: Laparoscopic trainer, not complete teleoperation loop; added-latency definition differs from RTT.

title: Influence of network latency and bandwidth on robot-assisted laparoscopic telesurgery: A pre-clinical experiment
network_focus: Latency; bandwidth; adaptive image compression; frame loss
main_finding: 108 animal operations over 3000 km explored 170–320-ms total latency and bandwidth down to <1 Mbps; image clarity was adaptively reduced as bandwidth narrowed; latency increased workload more than image-clarity reduction.
limitation: Authors call 320 ms acceptable for their system/tasks; should not be generalized as universal limit.

title: Impact of data compression and security devices on telesurgery systems
network_focus: Video bitrate; available bandwidth; security-device overhead
main_finding: hinotori tests used 120–20 Mbps image bitrates across 1-Gbps best-effort/IOWN and 100-Mbps guaranteed links; stable operation depended on adequate headroom; security devices added ≤2 ms in tested conditions.
limitation: Artificial-organ task and specific security/network devices.

title: Toward safe clinical deployment of remote robotic surgery in Japan: five-year validation of the hinotori system using 5G wireless communication
network_focus: 5G SA/NSA; QoS; congestion; video continuity; failover
main_finding: Summarizes >30 validations: QoS prevented packet loss/video degradation under heavy competing traffic; redundancy testing showed VPN reconnection in 5–11 s after simulated failures; Sub6 SA produced more predictable behavior than some alternatives.
limitation: Synthesis around one platform and Japanese deployment programme.

title: System-level evaluation of 5G standalone communication infrastructure for robotic telesurgery
venue: International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery
network_focus: 4G/5G NSA/SA; RTT; buffers; congestion; video freezes
main_finding: 5G SA configurations achieved sub-120-ms latency with stable video in controlled tests; 4G/high-bitrate NSA produced higher latency/freezes; SA Sub6 degraded beyond heavy background traffic (>400 Mbps in the reported setup).
limitation: Controlled system test; not a clinical trial and results are configuration-specific.

title: Construction of redundant communications to enhance safety against communication interruptions during robotic remote surgery
main_finding: Two commercial lines and redundant encoder interfaces were used; across 16 pig surgeries, 175 line switches were induced and no surgeon-detected abnormalities coincided with switching.
limitation: Animal study and specific redundancy design; brief switching-gap behavior can depend on path delay asymmetry.

title: Safety and reliability of telesurgery in China: a multicenter, single-arm, phase I clinical trial
network_focus: Clinical network metrics; codec; frame loss; seamless switching
main_finding: 18 patients across four hospitals: mean RTT 38.38±13.25 ms, jitter 0.39±0.29 ms, encode/decode latency 20.02±0.06 ms, code rate 12.77±0.57 Mbps, display latency 21.35±3.42 ms; no frame loss.
limitation: Single-arm clinical feasibility; system-specific network/video optimization.

title: Reliability of urological telesurgery compared with local surgery: multicentre randomised controlled trial
network_focus: Clinical network latency; display latency; frame loss; system malfunction
main_finding: 72 participants randomized; telesurgery was non-inferior to local surgery under trial conditions; telesurgery distances 1000–2800 km, mean RTT 20.1–47.5 ms and 0–1.5 lost frames per telesurgery.
limitation: Trial conditions were well-controlled; does not establish tolerance to degraded networks.

title: Feasibility and Safety of Cross-Regional 5G-Enabled Remote Robot-Assisted Laparoscopic Surgery: A Retrospective Case Series of 21 Patients
venue: International Journal of Medical Robotics and Computer Assisted Surgery 22:e70214
network_focus: Redundant 5G; RTT; jitter; loss; protocol thresholds
main_finding: 21 Toumai procedures over ~3700 km: mean RTT 37.7±5.6 ms, jitter 2.2±0.5 ms, no packet loss/interruption; preset local network criteria and backup carriers were used.
limitation: Retrospective; observed stable range does not validate failure thresholds.

title: Establishing an international clinical framework for telesurgery: the first bidirectional transatlantic procedure across a world-record distance
main_finding: Bidirectional procedures across >12,000 km reported mean latency ~196 ms, jitter 1 ms, packet loss 0.19%, and 100% connection uptime.
limitation: Small clinical report; platform/control architecture and delay definition matter.

title: A New Technological Approach to Robotic Telesurgery with Starlink: Safe Telesurgery
venue: Annals of Thoracic Surgery Short Reports 3:867–871
network_focus: LEO satellite; RTT variability; image disturbance
main_finding: Swine lung telesurgery over ~1000 km via Starlink reported average RTT ~130 ms and brief image/operation disturbances about every five minutes, possibly related to switching/weather.
limitation: Animal experiment; satellite conditions can vary temporally and causality of disturbances was not proven.

title: Real-world evaluation of low-earth-orbit satellite communication for surgical telementoring: implications for future robotic surgery
main_finding: One session averaged 34.4 ms latency and 2.51 Mbps, but the same setup next day reached 765-ms maximum latency and low-bitrate periods with marked quality deterioration; other configurations had intermittent freezing.
limitation: Telementoring rather than robot control; nonetheless strong evidence of LEO temporal variability.

title: Feasibility and safety evaluation of remote robotic surgery under high latency conditions based on satellite communication
main_finding: Two human liver resections used APSTAR-6D with average end-to-end latency 632 ms and low Mbps links; specialized high-delay control enabled completion.
limitation: Two cases and specialized control system; not evidence that ordinary telesurgery tolerates 632 ms.

title: The era of telesurgery: insights from ultra-long-distance Asia to Middle East human telesurgery robotic assisted radical prostatectomy
main_finding: Shanghai–Kuwait Toumai case reported average RTT 181.4 ms; fiber primary with 5G/wired backups and bedside robotic-surgeon takeover capability.
limitation: Single international case; deployment-specific cloud/routing architecture.

title: Safety and feasibility of telerobotic cholecystectomy via a 5G network: a prospective controlled clinical trial
main_finding: 20 remote cases over ~70 km reported average network delay 43.4 ms, jitter 4 ms, packet loss <1%, upload 98.3 Mbps and download 213 Mbps; later synthesis reports a ~3-s signal interruption triggering robot standby.
limitation: Delay terminology is study-specific; standby detail comes from later review.

title: Safety and feasibility of robot-assisted remote radical gastrectomy for gastric cancer based on 5G communication technology (FUTURE-04)
network_focus: Network RTT vs total delay; packet loss
main_finding: 27 cases over 15 km reported network RTT 31.6±3.8 ms but total delay 226.2±4.4 ms, showing that network RTT is not total teleoperation latency; packet loss <0.1%.
limitation: Short distance; total-delay decomposition is platform-specific.

title: Telerobotic partial nephrectomy and radical prostatectomy using a hybrid network: A single-center prospective experience
main_finding: 13 cases over ~25 km reported median latency 12 ms over fiber and 46 ms over 5G with no major network disruptions.
limitation: Single centre and short distance.

title: Application of 5G Remote Robotic-assisted Laparoscopy in Urological Surgery: A Small Sample Analysis
main_finding: 14 cases over 52 km reported 0% packet loss, 216.5 Mbps down/86.6 Mbps up, and study-defined minimum/maximum latency measures.
limitation: Small cohort; reported latency terms are not RTT.

title: RTP: A Transport Protocol for Real-Time Applications (RFC 3550)
main_finding: Defines RTP interarrival jitter from packet spacing relative to RTP timestamps and distinguishes transient congestion/jitter from persistent loss indicators.
limitation: Generic real-time media standard, not telesurgery-specific.

title: RTP Payload Format for H.264 Video (RFC 6184)
main_finding: A lost fragment can invalidate the remaining fragments of the same NAL unit; loss therefore does not map one-to-one to a dropped video frame.
limitation: Codec payload standard; actual decoder concealment is implementation-dependent.

title: RTP Payload Format for High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) (RFC 7798)
main_finding: Requires congestion responsiveness; real-time encoders can adapt bitrate via quantization, while scalable streams may drop enhancement-layer NAL units.
limitation: Generic media transport; telesurgical systems may use proprietary codecs.

title: RTP Retransmission Payload Format (RFC 4588)
main_finding: Retransmission can recover selected lost media packets but consumes bandwidth and time; it is useful only when retransmitted data can arrive before its playout deadline.
limitation: Generic RTP recovery mechanism.

title: WebRTC Forward Error Correction Requirements (RFC 8854)
main_finding: FEC proactively spends bandwidth; RTX/FEC retransmission is preferred when RTT fits the latency budget, while proactive FEC may be useful when waiting a round trip is too slow.
limitation: WebRTC guidance; not proof of a particular telesurgical implementation.

title: Congestion Control Requirements for Interactive Real-Time Media (RFC 8836)
network_focus: Low-delay media; jitter buffers; late data
main_finding: Interactive media needs low delay; moderate jitter can be absorbed by jitter buffers, but late real-time media may become useless.
limitation: Generic interactive-media requirements.

title: Self-Clocked Rate Adaptation for Multimedia (RFC 8298)
main_finding: SCReAM links congestion signals, RTP queue delay and loss events to a target media bitrate, illustrating how network conditions can drive encoder-rate changes.
limitation: One generic RTP congestion-control design, not a telesurgery requirement.

title: Error concealment schemes for H.264/AVC and H.265/HEVC video decoders
main_finding: Reviews/spans spatial, temporal and hybrid concealment strategies showing that decoded output after packet loss depends on concealment, not just loss rate.
limitation: Generic video coding evidence.

title: A study of packet loss effects on H.264 video quality
venue: Journal of Visual Communication and Image Representation
network_focus: H.264 packet loss; bitrate; visual quality
main_finding: Shows packet-loss impact depends on coding/bitrate and video-quality measurement; lower bitrate can sometimes trade source quality for improved loss resilience.
limitation: Non-surgical video; used only for codec-mechanism context.

title: On the Robustness of Temporal Vision-Language Models for Surgical Endoscopy Videos
network_focus: Downstream surgical AI under visual/packet-loss corruption
main_finding: Endo-C6 includes packet-loss bursts alongside defocus, haze, motion blur, shot noise and cautery smoke for temporal surgical/endoscopy VLM evaluation.
limitation: Corruption is applied at clip level; it does not establish a physical packet→codec→decoder mapping for a telesurgical stream.
